summary.headline: Borosil Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 9% YoY to INR 253.6 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 14.6% from 17.8% on West Asia input cost inflation.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 9% YoY to INR 253.6 crore, with Larah Opalware up 9.8% to INR 83.6 crore and glassware up 16.8% to INR 65.6 crore. Operating EBITDA (before investment income and one-time items) fell to INR 35.9 crore from INR 40.2 crore, with margin down to 14.6% from 17.8%, which management attributes mainly to fuel and packaging inflation from the West Asia conflict (about INR 10 crore net impact in Q1). Profit after tax fell to INR 12.8 crore from INR 17.4 crore, helped by royalty income of INR 4 crore but hurt by the absence of last year's INR 7.2 crore stamp duty reversal. Management guided to about 18% EBITDA margin for FY27 excluding other income, while acknowledging price pass-through realisations lag until Q2 onwards.

segments.name: Larah Opalware
segments.commentary: Sales INR 83.6 crore vs INR 76.2 crore, up 9.8%; management said growth was entirely volume-led with little price contribution. Price hikes taken but realisation expected from Q2.

segments.name: Glassware (borosilicate microwavables, serveware, tumblers, lunch boxes, storage)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 65.6 crore vs INR 56.2 crore, up 16.8%; management said growth was volume-led. Price increases of about 5-7% by category (sometimes higher) have been passed on with a lag.

segments.name: Non-glassware (small appliances, insulated bottles and flasks, cookware, kitchen essentials)
segments.commentary: Turnover INR 98.1 crore vs INR 94.2 crore, up 4.2%; BIS compliance continued to hit the Hydra flasks range, more than offset by growth in domestic appliances and stainless steel cookware.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 18% on the overall business, excluding other income; management framed the 18-20% range as steady-state without the West Asia impact, versus a historical 14-15%.
FY27 capex estimated at INR 125-150 crore, covering the borosilicate furnace expansion, the Bharuch glassware plant, possible solar projects and the opalware furnace rebuild.
FY27 depreciation expected at about INR 92 crore at consolidated level, including the Hydra plant.
Solar savings from Phase 3 expected at INR 27-28 crore at EBITDA level in FY27; net savings for next year not yet quantified.
Price realisations expected to kick in from Q2 and Q3 FY27; management declined to quantify margin improvement over the next two quarters.
Longer-term ROCE aspiration of 20-24% (also cited as 22%), with no timeline given; management declined to bridge current ~11% ROCE to that level in numbers.
Opalware revenue growth expected to continue at about 9%-type levels; management declined to endorse 15% growth for both segments.
capex_capacity: Third captive solar plant at Bikaner commissioned in Q1 FY27: 20 MWp with battery energy storage, first under Green Energy Open Access Regulations 2025; solar now meets about 61% of energy requirement.
Stylenest India (subsidiary) Hydra plant in Rajasthan: 2 double-wall vacuum flask lines started commercial production on 30 June 2026; third line expected in Q2 FY27.
Bharuch, Gujarat glassware plant (INR 42 crore capex) for jugs, jars and bottles, currently sourced at about INR 100 crore sales from BSL Bharuch; commissioning expected by end Q3 FY27.

Jaipur borosilicate pressware furnace expansion from 25 to 32 tons per day with a third forming line (INR 50 crore capex); current furnace utilisation about 90%; commissioning expected by end Q4 FY28.
Evaluating a further 6.5 MWp captive solar plant at Borosil and a 3-4 MWp plant at Stylenest for the Hydra facility.
Management said both glassware and Opalware are at full or about 90% capacity utilisation; capex on solar to date about INR 130 crore.
demand_pricing: Glassware and Opalware growth described as volume-led; price hikes of about 5-7% by category, not uniform, with realisation lagging.
Management said the price pass-through in Q1 was only about a couple of crore against an overall West Asia sales impact of about INR 12 crore.

Fuel cost as share of sales rose to 5.8% in Q1 FY27 from 2.9% a year earlier; Opalware fuel impact INR 6 crore reducing to about INR 1.5 crore a quarter and borosilicate impact INR 2.5 crore reducing to INR 60-70 lakh a quarter at current prices.
Chinese dumping in borosilicate glassware continues despite rupee depreciation and higher freight; anti-dumping investigation pending with authorities, with no timeline.
Whiteware about 10% of Opalware sales (vs under 5% last year), at margins below the regular range, so management is not pushing it.
Products available in over 24,000 retail outlets across general trade, modern retail, e-commerce and quick commerce.
